translations.idiomatic: If ritual institutions do not remain, there is nothing by which to govern.

sentences.zh: 眾之從上，猶水之居器也。

translations.literal: The multitude following those above is like water occupying a vessel.
translations.idiomatic: The multitude following those above is like water occupying a vessel.

sentences.zh: 故兆庶之情，信于所習；

translations.literal: Therefore the feelings of the common people trust in what they are accustomed to.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the feelings of the common people trust in what they are accustomed to.

sentences.zh: 習則心服其業，業服則謂之理然。

translations.literal: Once accustomed, their minds submit to their tasks; when their tasks are accepted, they call it naturally right.
translations.idiomatic: Once accustomed, their minds submit to their tasks; when their tasks are accepted, they call it naturally right.

sentences.zh: 是以君人必慎所教，班其政刑一切之務，分宅百姓，各授四職，能令稟命之者不肅而安，忽然忘異，莫有遷志。

translations.literal: Therefore one who rules people must be careful about what he teaches, distributes all the affairs of government and punishments, divides dwellings among the hundred surnames, and assigns each of the four occupations. He can make those who receive commands be at ease without sternness, suddenly forget differences, and have no mind to shift.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore one who rules people must be careful about what he teaches, distributes all the affairs of government and punishments, divides dwellings among the hundred surnames, and assigns each of the four occupations. He can make those who receive commands be at ease without sternness, suddenly forget differences, and have no mind to shift.

sentences.zh: 況於據在三之尊，懷所隆之情，敦以為訓者哉！

translations.literal: How much more is this true for one who occupies honor among the Three, holds feelings about what should be exalted, and treats them seriously as instruction.
translations.idiomatic: How much more is this true for one who occupies honor among the Three, holds feelings about what should be exalted, and treats them seriously as instruction.

sentences.zh: 斯乃昏明所階，不可不審。

translations.literal: This is the step by which darkness or clarity proceeds, and it must be examined carefully.
translations.idiomatic: This is the step by which darkness or clarity proceeds, and it must be examined carefully.

sentences.zh: 夫盈欲可損而未可絕有也，過用可節而未可謂無貴也。

translations.literal: Overflowing desire may be reduced, but being cannot be cut off; excessive use may be regulated, but it cannot be said that there is nothing valuable.
translations.idiomatic: Overflowing desire may be reduced, but being cannot be cut off; excessive use may be regulated, but it cannot be said that there is nothing valuable.

sentences.zh: 蓋有講言之具者，深列有形之故，盛稱空無之美。

translations.literal: Those equipped for discourse deeply arrayed the causes of what has form and grandly praised the beauty of emptiness and nonbeing.
translations.idiomatic: Those equipped for discourse deeply arrayed the causes of what has form and grandly praised the beauty of emptiness and nonbeing.

sentences.zh: 形器之故有征，空無之義難檢，辯巧之文可悅，似象之言足惑，眾聽眩焉，溺其成說。

translations.literal: The causes of forms and vessels have evidence; the meaning of emptiness and nonbeing is hard to check. Cleverly argued writings can delight, and words resembling images are enough to confuse, so the many listeners were dazzled and drowned in these completed doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: The causes of forms and vessels have evidence; the meaning of emptiness and nonbeing is hard to check. Cleverly argued writings can delight, and words resembling images are enough to confuse, so the many listeners were dazzled and drowned in these completed doctrines.

sentences.zh: 雖頗有異此心者，辭不獲濟，屈於所狎，因謂虛無之理，誠不可蓋。

translations.literal: Although some had minds that differed from this, their words could not prevail; they yielded to what was familiar, and accordingly said that the principle of emptiness and nonbeing truly could not be covered over.
translations.idiomatic: Although some had minds that differed from this, their words could not prevail; they yielded to what was familiar, and accordingly said that the principle of emptiness and nonbeing truly could not be covered over.

sentences.zh: 唱而有和，多往弗反，遂薄綜世之務，賤功烈之用，高浮游之業，埤經實之賢。

translations.literal: When one sang out, others harmonized; many went forth and did not return. They then slighted the work of managing the age, devalued the use of achievements, elevated the occupation of drifting idly, and lowered worthies of canonical substance.
translations.idiomatic: When one sang out, others harmonized; many went forth and did not return. They then slighted the work of managing the age, devalued the use of achievements, elevated the occupation of drifting idly, and lowered worthies of canonical substance.

sentences.zh: 人情所殉，篤夫名利。

translations.literal: What human feelings die for is especially name and profit.
translations.idiomatic: What human feelings die for is especially name and profit.

sentences.zh: 於是文者衍其辭，訥者贊其旨，染其眾也。

translations.literal: Thereupon those skilled in writing elaborated their words, and those slow of speech praised their intent, staining the multitude with it.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon those skilled in writing elaborated their words, and those slow of speech praised their intent, staining the multitude with it.

sentences.zh: 是以立言藉於虛無，謂之玄妙；

translations.literal: Thus setting up words by relying on emptiness and nonbeing was called mysterious subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: Thus setting up words by relying on emptiness and nonbeing was called mysterious subtlety.

sentences.zh: 處官不親所司，謂之雅遠；

translations.literal: Holding office without personally attending to one's responsibilities was called elegant remoteness.
translations.idiomatic: Holding office without personally attending to one's responsibilities was called elegant remoteness.

sentences.zh: 奉身散其廉操，謂之曠達。

translations.literal: Supporting oneself while scattering one's integrity and conduct was called broad-minded freedom.
translations.idiomatic: Supporting oneself while scattering one's integrity and conduct was called broad-minded freedom.

sentences.zh: 故砥礪之風，彌以陵遲。

translations.literal: Therefore the custom of whetting and disciplining oneself declined all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the custom of whetting and disciplining oneself declined all the more.

sentences.zh: 放者因斯，或悖吉凶之禮，而忽容止之表，瀆棄長幼之序，混漫貴賤之級。

translations.literal: The unrestrained used this as their basis, sometimes violating the rituals of auspicious and inauspicious occasions, neglecting the outward signs of bearing and deportment, profaning and abandoning the order of elder and younger, and confusing and blurring the ranks of noble and base.
translations.idiomatic: The unrestrained used this as their basis, sometimes violating the rituals of auspicious and inauspicious occasions, neglecting the outward signs of bearing and deportment, profaning and abandoning the order of elder and younger, and confusing and blurring the ranks of noble and base.

sentences.zh: 其甚者至於裸裎，言笑忘宜，以不惜為弘，士行又虧矣。

translations.literal: The worst of them even reached naked exposure, forgot what was proper in speech and laughter, took lack of restraint as magnanimity, and gentlemanly conduct was further damaged.
translations.idiomatic: The worst of them even reached naked exposure, forgot what was proper in speech and laughter, took lack of restraint as magnanimity, and gentlemanly conduct was further damaged.

sentences.zh: 老子既著五千之文，表摭穢雜之弊，甄舉靜一之義，有以令人釋然自夷，合于《易》之《損》、《謙》、《艮》、《節》之旨。

translations.literal: Laozi wrote the text of five thousand words, displayed and picked out the harms of filth and mixture, and selected and raised the meaning of stillness and unity, so that people could be released and level themselves. This accords with the meanings of Decrease, Modesty, Keeping Still, and Regulation in the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Laozi wrote the text of five thousand words, displayed and picked out the harms of filth and mixture, and selected and raised the meaning of stillness and unity, so that people could be released and level themselves. This accords with the meanings of Decrease, Modesty, Keeping Still, and Regulation in the Changes.

sentences.zh: 而靜一守本，無虛無之謂也；

translations.literal: But stillness, unity, and guarding the root do not mean emptiness and nonbeing.
translations.idiomatic: But stillness, unity, and guarding the root do not mean emptiness and nonbeing.

sentences.zh: 《損》《艮》之屬，蓋君子之一道，非《易》之所以為體守本無也。

translations.literal: Decrease, Keeping Still, and the like are one way of the gentleman; they are not the way by which the Changes makes guarding root nonbeing its substance.
translations.idiomatic: Decrease, Keeping Still, and the like are one way of the gentleman; they are not the way by which the Changes makes guarding root nonbeing its substance.

sentences.zh: 觀老子之書雖博有所經，而云「有生於無」，以虛為主，偏立一家之辭，豈有以而然哉！

translations.literal: Looking at Laozi's book, although it broadly passes through many things, it says, "Being is born from nonbeing," takes emptiness as its master, and partially establishes the words of one school. How could there be a sufficient reason for this?
translations.idiomatic: Looking at Laozi's book, although it broadly passes through many things, it says, "Being is born from nonbeing," takes emptiness as its master, and partially establishes the words of one school. How could there be a sufficient reason for this?

sentences.zh: 人之既生，以保生為全，全之所階，以順感為務。

translations.literal: Once people have been born, they take preserving life as wholeness; the step to wholeness takes responding in accord as its task.
translations.idiomatic: Once people have been born, they take preserving life as wholeness; the step to wholeness takes responding in accord as its task.

sentences.zh: 若味近以虧業，則沈溺之釁興；

translations.literal: If one savors what is near and thereby damages one's work, then the trouble of sinking and drowning arises.
translations.idiomatic: If one savors what is near and thereby damages one's work, then the trouble of sinking and drowning arises.

sentences.zh: 懷末以忘本，則天理之真滅。

translations.literal: If one cherishes the branch and forgets the root, then the truth of heavenly principle is extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: If one cherishes the branch and forgets the root, then the truth of heavenly principle is extinguished.

sentences.zh: 故動之所交，存亡之會也。

translations.literal: Therefore what action engages is the meeting point of survival and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore what action engages is the meeting point of survival and ruin.

sentences.zh: 夫有非有，於無非無；

translations.literal: Being is not merely being; in relation to nonbeing it is not nonbeing.
translations.idiomatic: Being is not merely being; in relation to nonbeing it is not nonbeing.

sentences.zh: 于無非無，於有非有。

translations.literal: In relation to nonbeing it is not nonbeing, and in relation to being it is not merely being.
translations.idiomatic: In relation to nonbeing it is not nonbeing, and in relation to being it is not merely being.

sentences.zh: 是以申縱播之累，而著貴無之文。

translations.literal: Therefore Laozi extended the harms of indulgence and diffusion, and wrote a text that honored nonbeing.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Laozi extended the harms of indulgence and diffusion, and wrote a text that honored nonbeing.

sentences.zh: 將以絕所非之盈謬，存大善之中節，收流遁於既過，反澄正於胸懷。

translations.literal: He was about to cut off the overflowing errors he rejected, preserve the central measure of great goodness, gather back what had flowed away after going too far, and return clarity and correctness to the breast.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to cut off the overflowing errors he rejected, preserve the central measure of great goodness, gather back what had flowed away after going too far, and return clarity and correctness to the breast.

sentences.zh: 宜其以無為辭，而旨在全有，故其辭曰「以為文不足」。

translations.literal: It is fitting that he used nonbeing as his wording while his intent lay in making being whole; therefore his words say, "I consider writing insufficient."
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting that he used nonbeing as his wording while his intent lay in making being whole; therefore his words say, "I consider writing insufficient."

sentences.zh: 若斯，則是所寄之塗，一方之言也。

translations.literal: If it is like this, then this is a path on which something was lodged, the words of one side.
translations.idiomatic: If it is like this, then this is a path on which something was lodged, the words of one side.

sentences.zh: 若謂至理信以無為宗，則偏而害當矣。

translations.literal: If one says that the highest principle truly takes nonbeing as its ancestor, then this is partial and harms what is appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: If one says that the highest principle truly takes nonbeing as its ancestor, then this is partial and harms what is appropriate.

sentences.zh: 先賢達識，以非所滯，示之深論。

translations.literal: Earlier worthies of penetrating understanding, because they were not stuck there, showed this in deep arguments.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier worthies of penetrating understanding, because they were not stuck there, showed this in deep arguments.

sentences.zh: 惟班固著難，未足折其情。

translations.literal: Only Ban Gu wrote objections, but they were not sufficient to break its appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Only Ban Gu wrote objections, but they were not sufficient to break its appeal.

sentences.zh: 孫卿、楊雄大體抑之，猶偏有所許。

translations.literal: Xunzi and Yang Xiong suppressed it in general outline, yet still partly allowed it.
translations.idiomatic: Xunzi and Yang Xiong suppressed it in general outline, yet still partly allowed it.

sentences.zh: 而虛無之言，日以廣衍，眾家扇起，各列其說。

translations.literal: But the words of emptiness and nonbeing spread more widely day by day, and the many schools stirred one another up, each setting forth its theory.
translations.idiomatic: But the words of emptiness and nonbeing spread more widely day by day, and the many schools stirred one another up, each setting forth its theory.

sentences.zh: 上及造化，下被萬事，莫不貴無，所存僉同。

translations.literal: Above they reached creation and transformation, below they covered the ten thousand affairs; there was nothing in which they did not honor nonbeing, and what they preserved was all the same.
translations.idiomatic: Above they reached creation and transformation, below they covered the ten thousand affairs; there was nothing in which they did not honor nonbeing, and what they preserved was all the same.

sentences.zh: 情以眾固，乃號凡有之理皆義之埤者，薄而鄙焉。

translations.literal: Because feeling was made firm by the crowd, they then called every principle of being a low supplement to meaning and treated it as slight and contemptible.
translations.idiomatic: Because feeling was made firm by the crowd, they then called every principle of being a low supplement to meaning and treated it as slight and contemptible.

sentences.zh: 辯論人倫及經明之業，遂易門肆。

translations.literal: Debating human relations and the work of making the classics clear accordingly changed gates and marketplaces.
translations.idiomatic: Debating human relations and the work of making the classics clear accordingly changed gates and marketplaces.

sentences.zh: 頠用矍然，申其所懷，而攻者盈集。

translations.literal: Pei Wei therefore became alarmed and expressed what he held in mind, but attackers gathered in numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Wei therefore became alarmed and expressed what he held in mind, but attackers gathered in numbers.

sentences.zh: 或以為一時口言。

translations.literal: Some thought it was only words spoken for the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Some thought it was only words spoken for the moment.

sentences.zh: 有客幸過，咸見命著文，擿列虛無不允之征。

translations.literal: When guests happened to visit, all urged him to write an essay and pick out and list the proofs that emptiness and nonbeing were not sound.
translations.idiomatic: When guests happened to visit, all urged him to write an essay and pick out and list the proofs that emptiness and nonbeing were not sound.

sentences.zh: 若未能每事釋正，則無家之義弗可奪也。

translations.literal: If he could not explain and correct each matter, then the meaning of the school of nonbeing could not be seized away.
translations.idiomatic: If he could not explain and correct each matter, then the meaning of the school of nonbeing could not be seized away.

sentences.zh: 頠退而思之，雖君子宅情，無求於顯，及其立言，在乎達旨而已。

translations.literal: Pei Wei withdrew and thought about it. Although a gentleman lodges his feelings and does not seek display, when it comes to establishing words, it only lies in making the intent clear.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Wei withdrew and thought about it. Although a gentleman lodges his feelings and does not seek display, when it comes to establishing words, it only lies in making the intent clear.

sentences.zh: 然去聖久遠，異同紛糾，苟少有仿佛，可以崇濟先典，扶明大業，有益於時，則惟患言之不能，焉得靜默，及未舉一隅，略示所存而已哉！

translations.literal: Yet the age was long distant from the sages, and differences and agreements were tangled. If there were even a slight resemblance by which one could exalt and aid the former canons, support and clarify the great enterprise, and benefit the time, then one should worry only that one could not say it. How could one remain silent, or merely point to one corner and sketch what one preserved?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the age was long distant from the sages, and differences and agreements were tangled. If there were even a slight resemblance by which one could exalt and aid the former canons, support and clarify the great enterprise, and benefit the time, then one should worry only that one could not say it. How could one remain silent, or merely point to one corner and sketch what one preserved?

sentences.zh: 夫至無者無以能生，故始生者自生也。

translations.literal: Utter nonbeing has no means by which it can generate life; therefore what first produces life produces itself.
translations.idiomatic: Utter nonbeing has no means by which it can generate life; therefore what first produces life produces itself.

sentences.zh: 自生而必體有，則有遺而生虧矣。

translations.literal: If what produces itself must embody being, then if being is left behind, production is deficient.
translations.idiomatic: If what produces itself must embody being, then if being is left behind, production is deficient.

sentences.zh: 生以有為已分，則虛無是有之所謂遺者也。

translations.literal: Since production takes being as its own allotment, emptiness and nonbeing are what being calls something left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Since production takes being as its own allotment, emptiness and nonbeing are what being calls something left behind.

sentences.zh: 故養既化之有，非無用之所能全也；

translations.literal: Therefore nourishing being after it has transformed is not something the function of nonbeing can make whole.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore nourishing being after it has transformed is not something the function of nonbeing can make whole.

sentences.zh: 理既有之眾，非無為之所能循也。

translations.literal: Ordering the multitude after it already exists is not something nonaction can follow through on.
translations.idiomatic: Ordering the multitude after it already exists is not something nonaction can follow through on.

sentences.zh: 心非事也，而制事必由於心，然不可以制事以非事，謂心為無也。

translations.literal: The mind is not an affair, yet regulating affairs must come from the mind; but one cannot, because regulating affairs is not itself an affair, call the mind nonbeing.
translations.idiomatic: The mind is not an affair, yet regulating affairs must come from the mind; but one cannot, because regulating affairs is not itself an affair, call the mind nonbeing.

sentences.zh: 匠非器也，而制器必須於匠，然不可以制器以非器，謂匠非有也。

translations.literal: The artisan is not the vessel, yet making vessels must require the artisan; but one cannot, because making vessels is not itself the vessel, say that the artisan is not being.
translations.idiomatic: The artisan is not the vessel, yet making vessels must require the artisan; but one cannot, because making vessels is not itself the vessel, say that the artisan is not being.

sentences.zh: 是以欲收重泉之鱗，非偃息之所能獲也；

translations.literal: Therefore if one wants to catch fish in the deep springs, it is not something lying still can obtain.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore if one wants to catch fish in the deep springs, it is not something lying still can obtain.

sentences.zh: 隕高墉之禽，非靜拱之所能捷也；

translations.literal: If one wants to bring down birds from high walls, it is not something standing quietly with folded hands can swiftly accomplish.
translations.idiomatic: If one wants to bring down birds from high walls, it is not something standing quietly with folded hands can swiftly accomplish.

sentences.zh: 審投弦餌之用，非無知之所能覽也。

translations.literal: Examining the use of casting lines and bait is not something without knowledge can perceive.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the use of casting lines and bait is not something without knowledge can perceive.

sentences.zh: 由此而觀，濟有者皆有也，虛無奚益於已有之群生哉！

translations.literal: Seen from this, what assists being is all being. What benefit do emptiness and nonbeing have for the multitude of living beings that already exist?
translations.idiomatic: Seen from this, what assists being is all being. What benefit do emptiness and nonbeing have for the multitude of living beings that already exist?

sentences.zh: 王衍之徒攻難交至，並莫能屈。

translations.literal: Wang Yan's clique besieged him with objections, yet none could break his argument.
translations.idiomatic: The qingtan circle attacked his thesis from every side without refuting it.

sentences.zh: 又著《辯才論》，古今精義皆辨釋焉，未成而遇禍。

translations.literal: He also composed the "Treatise on Eloquence," clarifying every subtle point ancient and modern; he did not finish it before catastrophe struck.
translations.idiomatic: His unfinished "Treatise on Eloquence" surveyed classical debates but death cut it short.

sentences.zh: 初，趙王倫諂事賈后，頠甚惡之，倫數求官，頠與張華復固執不許，由是深為倫所怨。

translations.literal: At first the Prince of Zhao, Sima Lun, fawned on Empress Jia; Yi loathed him. Lun repeatedly sought promotion; Yi and Zhang Hua steadfastly refused—thereby earning Lun's bitter hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun curried Jia Nanfeng's favor while Yi and Zhang Hua blocked his offices, planting a deadly grudge.

sentences.zh: 倫又潛懷篡逆，欲先除朝望，因廢賈后之際遂誅之，時年三十四。

translations.literal: Lun also nursed usurpation: wishing first to eliminate eminent ministers, he executed Yi while deposing the empress; Yi was thirty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Lun used Jia's fall as cover to murder Yi at thirty-four while plotting a coup.

sentences.zh: 二子嵩、該，倫亦欲害之。

translations.literal: His sons Song and Gai—Lun meant to kill them too.
translations.idiomatic: Lun targeted Yi's sons Song and Gai next.

sentences.zh: 梁王肜、東海王越稱頠父秀有勳王室，配食太廟，不宜滅其後嗣，故得不死，徙帶方；

translations.literal: Princes Sima Yong of Liang and Sima Yue of Donghai declared that Yi's father Xiu had served the dynasty and received offerings in the Grand Temple—his line must not be extinguished—so the boys lived on, banished to Daifang.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Donghai princes cited Xiu's temple honors to spare the sons, exiling them to Liaodong instead.

sentences.zh: 惠帝反正，追復頠本官，改葬以卿禮，諡曰成。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui was restored, Yi's offices were posthumously reinstated; he was reburied with ministerial ceremony and titled Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Hui's restoration Yi won reinstatement, a proper reburial, and the posthumous name Cheng.

sentences.zh: 以嵩嗣爵，為中書黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Song inherited the title and became palace attendant and palace secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The marquisate passed to Song in the central secretariat.

sentences.zh: 該出後從伯凱，為散騎常侍，並為乞活賊陳午所害。

translations.literal: Gai had been posthumously adopted to uncle Kai; he was supernumerary attendant until both brothers fell to Chen Wu's Qi Huo band.
translations.idiomatic: Adopted heir Gai died beside Song when Chen Wu's refugee warriors slaughtered them.

sentences.zh: 秀從弟楷

translations.literal: Pei Kai, Xiu's younger cousin
translations.idiomatic: Pei Kai—cousin to Pei Xiu

sentences.zh: =楷字叔則。

translations.literal: Kai, courtesy name Shuzé.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Kai, whose courtesy name was Shuzé,

sentences.zh: 父徽，魏冀州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Wei had been Governor of Jizhou under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Father Pei Wei governed Ji province for Wei.

sentences.zh: 楷明悟有識量，弱冠知名，尤精《老》、《易》，少與王戎齊名。

translations.literal: Kai was lucid and discerning, with breadth of judgment; before age twenty he was famous, especially in the Laozi and Changes, and was paired in renown with Wang Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Celebrated before twenty, he mastered the Daoist classics alongside Wang Rong.

sentences.zh: 鍾會薦之于文帝，辟相國掾，遷尚書郎。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui recommended him to Emperor Wen; Kai became aide to the minister of state and rose to gentleman of the palace secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui's referral brought him into Sima Zhao's bureau and the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 賈充改定律令，以楷為定科郎。

translations.literal: When Jia Chong revised statutes, Kai served as the drafter charged with fixing each legal article.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong's law revision named Kai specialist for codifying clauses.

sentences.zh: 事畢，詔楷於御前執讀，平議當否。

translations.literal: When the code was done, an edict ordered Kai to read it aloud before the throne and debate whether each clause fit.
translations.idiomatic: At court he read the new code aloud for imperial scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 楷善宣吐，左右屬目，聽者忘倦。

translations.literal: Kai spoke with luminous clarity; attendants hung on every word and listeners forgot fatigue.
translations.idiomatic: His exposition captivated the hall.

sentences.zh: 武帝為撫軍，妙選僚采，以楷為參軍事。

translations.literal: While Emperor Wu still served as General Who Supports the Army, he chose Kai as military administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan made him staff adviser during the princely generalship.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎缺，文帝問其人於鍾會。

translations.literal: The personnel director post stood empty; Emperor Wen asked Zhong Hui whom to appoint.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao asked Zhong Hui who should head personnel.

sentences.zh: 會曰：「裴楷清通，王戎簡要，皆其選也。」

translations.literal: Hui replied: "Pei Kai is lucid and penetrating; Wang Rong concise and essential—either suits the post."
translations.idiomatic: "Pei Kai or Wang Rong," said Zhong Hui, "both fit."

sentences.zh: 於是以楷為吏部郎。

translations.literal: Thereupon Kai became Director of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Kai received the appointment.

sentences.zh: 楷風神高邁，容儀俊爽，博涉群書，特精理義，時人謂之「玉人」，又稱「見裴叔則如近玉山，映照人也」。

translations.literal: Kai's spirit seemed borne on the wind; his face handsome and bright; he read widely and plumbed doctrine—people called him the "jade man" and said that meeting Pei Shuzé felt like nearing a jade mountain blazing with light.
translations.idiomatic: His aura and learning earned the nickname "jade man"—seeing him was likened to climbing a luminous jade peak.

sentences.zh: 轉中書郎，出入宮省，見者肅然改容。

translations.literal: Transferred to palace secretariat gentleman, he passed through palace gates so strikingly that onlookers straightened their bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Palace corridors fell silent when he passed.

sentences.zh: 武帝初登阼，探策以卜世數多少，而得一，帝不悅，群臣失色，莫有言者。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu first mounted the throne he drew oracle slips on dynastic longevity and drew "one"; the emperor frowned, ministers paled, none spoke.
translations.idiomatic: An ill-omened slip "one" from the imperial divination silenced the court.

sentences.zh: 楷正容儀，和其聲氣，從容進曰：「臣聞天得一以清，地得一以甯，王侯得一以為天下貞。」

translations.literal: Kai corrected his bearing, harmonized his voice and breath, and calmly advanced, saying, "I have heard that Heaven obtains the One and is clear, Earth obtains the One and is tranquil, and kings and lords obtain the One and become the rectitude of all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Kai corrected his bearing, harmonized his voice and breath, and calmly advanced, saying, "I have heard that Heaven obtains the One and is clear, Earth obtains the One and is tranquil, and kings and lords obtain the One and become the rectitude of all under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 武帝大悅，群臣皆稱萬歲。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu rejoiced; everyone shouted long live the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor brightened and the hall cheered.

sentences.zh: 俄拜散騎侍郎，累遷散騎常侍、河內太守，入為屯騎校尉、右軍將軍，轉侍中。

translations.literal: Soon he was supernumerary gentleman, then attendant, governor of Henei, colonel of household troops, general of the right guard, and palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Promotions swept him through Henei, camp command, the right guard, and back to attendant.

sentences.zh: 石崇以功臣子有才氣，與楷志趣各異，不與之交。

translations.literal: Shi Chong, proud son of a merit family, disagreed with Kai's tastes and kept his distance.
translations.idiomatic: The meritor Shi Chong avoided Kai on temperament.

sentences.zh: 長水校尉孫季舒嘗與崇酣燕，慢傲過度，崇欲表免之。

translations.literal: Colonel Sun Jishu once drank riotously with Chong, insulting others grossly; Chong planned to memorialize his dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jishu's drunken arrogance at Chong's banquet nearly cost him his post.

sentences.zh: 楷聞之，謂崇曰：「足下飲人狂藥，責人正禮，不亦乖乎！」

translations.literal: Kai told Chong: "You pour reckless wine yet demand ritual propriety—is that not perverse!"
translations.idiomatic: "You ply guests with reckless wine," Kai said, "then fault their manners—how absurd?"

sentences.zh: 崇乃止。

translations.literal: Chong dropped the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Chong relented.

sentences.zh: 楷性寬厚，與物無忤。

translations.literal: Kai was tolerant and magnanimous; he contended with nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Genial and conciliatory, he picked no quarrels.

sentences.zh: 不持儉素，每游榮貴，輒取其珍玩。

translations.literal: He did not affect austerity; visiting grandees he accepted their finest curios.
translations.idiomatic: He freely accepted gifts from the mighty.

sentences.zh: 雖車馬器服，宿昔之間，便以施諸窮乏。

translations.literal: Carriages, robes, vessels—overnight he gave them to the needy.
translations.idiomatic: By morning those luxuries reached the poor.

sentences.zh: 嘗營別宅，其從兄衍見而悅之，即以宅與衍。

translations.literal: He built a villa; cousin Wang Yan coveted it, so Kai gave him the house outright.
translations.idiomatic: Yan admired his new manor; Kai signed it over.

sentences.zh: 梁、趙二王，國之近屬，貴重當時，楷歲請二國租錢百萬，以散親族。

translations.literal: The Liang and Zhao princes were imperial kin of the highest rank; Kai annually took one million cash from their rents for kin.
translations.idiomatic: He diverted a million coins yearly from those princely estates to aid relatives.

sentences.zh: 人或譏之，楷曰：「損有餘以補不足，天之道也。」

translations.literal: Critics sneered; Kai answered: "Taking from surplus to aid deficiency—that is Heaven's Way."
translations.idiomatic: "Redistribution follows Heaven," he replied.

sentences.zh: 安於毀譽，其行己任率，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Untroubled by praise or blame, he lived candidly—always thus.
translations.idiomatic: He shrugged at gossip and followed instinct.

sentences.zh: 與山濤、和嶠並以盛德居位，帝嘗問曰：「朕應天順時，海內更始，天下風聲，何得何失？」

translations.literal: Together with Shan Tao and He Jiao, he held office with abundant virtue. The emperor once asked, "I respond to Heaven and follow the time, and within the seas there is a new beginning. In the voices of custom throughout the realm, what has been gained and what has been lost?"
translations.idiomatic: Together with Shan Tao and He Jiao, he held office with abundant virtue. The emperor once asked, "I respond to Heaven and follow the time, and within the seas there is a new beginning. In the voices of custom throughout the realm, what has been gained and what has been lost?"

sentences.zh: 楷對曰：「陛下受命，四海承風，所以未比德於堯舜者，但以賈充之徒尚在朝耳。

translations.literal: Kai replied, "Your Majesty has received the mandate, and the four seas follow your influence. The reason your virtue is not yet compared with Yao and Shun is only that the likes of Jia Chong are still at court.
translations.idiomatic: Kai replied, "Your Majesty has received the mandate, and the four seas follow your influence. The reason your virtue is not yet compared with Yao and Shun is only that the likes of Jia Chong are still at court.

sentences.zh: 方宜引天下賢人，與弘正道，不宜示人以私。」

translations.literal: Just now you should draw in worthy men from all under Heaven and with them broaden the correct Way; you should not show people private favor."
translations.idiomatic: Just now you should draw in worthy men from all under Heaven and with them broaden the correct Way; you should not show people private favor."

sentences.zh: 時任愷、庾純亦以充為言，帝乃出充為關中都督。

translations.literal: Ren Kai and Yu Chun echoed him; the emperor posted Chong to frontier command.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Kai and Yu Chun echoed him until the emperor reassigned Chong as Guanzhong area commander.

sentences.zh: 充納女于太子，乃止。

translations.literal: Chong married his daughter to the crown prince, and [the transfer] then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Chong betrothed his daughter to the crown prince, so the transfer was cancelled.

sentences.zh: 平吳之後，帝方修太平之化，每延公卿，與論政道。

translations.literal: After Wu fell the emperor cultivated Great Peace, hosting ministers to debate policy.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying Wu opened seminars on governance.

sentences.zh: 楷陳三五之風，次敘漢魏盛衰之跡。

translations.literal: Kai traced the Three August Ones and Five Lords, then Han and Wei's rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured on antiquity's golden ages versus Han-Wei cycles.

sentences.zh: 帝稱善，坐者嘆服焉。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him; listeners sighed admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved and the assembly marveled.

sentences.zh: 楷子瓚娶楊駿女，然楷素輕駿，與之不平。

translations.literal: Kai's son Zan married Yang Jun's daughter though Kai despised Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Zan's marriage to Jun's daughter strained Kai's contempt for Jun.

sentences.zh: 駿既執政，乃轉為衛尉，遷太子少師，優遊無事，默如也。

translations.literal: Once Jun dominated court, Kai became minister of guards and junior tutor—idle, mute.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sidelined him as ceremonial tutor with nothing to do.

sentences.zh: 及駿誅，楷以婚親收付廷尉，將加法。

translations.literal: When Jun fell, Kai as in-law went to the Ministry of Justice for sentencing.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's purge dragged Kai toward execution.

sentences.zh: 是日事倉卒，誅戮縱橫，眾人為之震恐。

translations.literal: That day slaughter raced everywhere—courtiers panicked.
translations.idiomatic: Sudden killings terrified Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 楷容色不變，舉動自若，索紙筆與親故書。

translations.literal: Kai never flinched; calmly he borrowed brush and wrote farewell letters.
translations.idiomatic: He calmly penned letters while awaiting death.

sentences.zh: 賴侍中傅祗救護得免，猶坐去官。

translations.literal: Thanks to Palace Attendant Fu Zhi's rescue he escaped execution, though he still lost office for it.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi intervened; Kai merely lost rank.

sentences.zh: 太保衛瓘、太宰亮稱楷貞正不阿附，宜蒙爵土，乃封臨海侯，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: Grand tutors Wei Guan and Sima Liang praised Kai's integrity—he deserved a fief—and named him Marquis of Linhai with two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan and Sima Liang restored him as marquis of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 代楚王瑋為北軍中候，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He replaced Prince Chu Wei as colonel of the northern armies plus supernumerary attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He took the northern army colonelcy alongside attendant honors.

sentences.zh: 瑋怨瓘、亮斥己任楷，楷聞之，不敢拜，轉為尚書。

translations.literal: Wei resented Guan and Liang for ousting him for Kai; Kai declined the post and became minister of state.
translations.idiomatic: Wei blamed Kai for stealing his command; Kai fled upward to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 楷長子輿先娶亮女，女適衛瓘子，楷慮內難未已，求出外鎮，除安南將軍、假節、都督荊州諸軍事，垂當發而瑋果矯詔誅亮、瓘。

translations.literal: Kai's heir Yu had married Sima Liang's daughter while Yu's wife joined Wei Guan's son—fearing civil war Kai sought a province; made southern commander with staff for Jingzhou—just as he prepared to march, Wei forged an edict killing Liang and Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage ties to both factions drove Kai toward Jingzhou—Wei's forged orders struck first.

sentences.zh: 瑋以楷前奪己中候，又與亮、瓘婚親，密遣討楷。

translations.literal: Wei because Kai had earlier displaced him from Central Commander and was also marriage kin to Liang and Guan secretly sent forces against Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent killers after Kai for family links to his victims.

sentences.zh: 楷素知瑋有望于己，聞有變，單車入城，匿于妻父王渾家，與亮小子一夜八徙，故得免難。

translations.literal: Kai had always known Wei bore him ill will; hearing of the upheaval, he drove alone into the city and hid in his father-in-law Wang Hun's house; with Liang's youngest son he moved eight times in one night—thus he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: He dodged patrols by hiding with Wang Hun and Liang's orphan.

sentences.zh: 瑋既伏誅，以楷為中書令，加侍中，與張華、王戎並管機要。

translations.literal: After Wei died Kai directed the palace secretariat with Zhang Hua and Wang Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei fell and Kai joined Zhang Hua and Wang Rong at power's core.

sentences.zh: 楷有渴利疾，不樂處勢。

translations.literal: Kai suffered wasting thirst and loathed heavy responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Diabetes-like thirst made central office unbearable.

sentences.zh: 王渾為楷請曰：「楷受先帝拔擢之恩，復蒙陛下寵遇，誠竭節之秋也。

translations.literal: Wang Hun made a request on Kai's behalf, saying, "Kai received the grace of being promoted by the former emperor and again has received Your Majesty's favor and treatment; truly this is the autumn for exhausting his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun made a request on Kai's behalf, saying, "Kai received the grace of being promoted by the former emperor and again has received Your Majesty's favor and treatment; truly this is the autumn for exhausting his integrity.

sentences.zh: 然楷性不競於物，昔為常侍，求出為河內太守；

translations.literal: Yet Kai's nature does not compete with things. Formerly, when he was Regular Attendant, he sought to go out as Grand Administrator of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Kai's nature does not compete with things. Formerly, when he was Regular Attendant, he sought to go out as Grand Administrator of Henei.

sentences.zh: 後為侍中，復求出為河南尹；

translations.literal: Later, when he was Palace Attendant, he again sought to go out as Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he was Palace Attendant, he again sought to go out as Governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 與楊駿不平，求為衛尉；

translations.literal: When he was not on good terms with Yang Jun, he sought to become Chamberlain for the Palace Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When he was not on good terms with Yang Jun, he sought to become Chamberlain for the Palace Garrison.

sentences.zh: 及轉東宮，班在時類之下，安於淡退，有識有以見其心也。

translations.literal: When he was transferred to the Eastern Palace, his rank was below those of his time and class, yet he was at ease in plain withdrawal. Those with understanding had means to see his mind.
translations.idiomatic: When he was transferred to the Eastern Palace, his rank was below those of his time and class, yet he was at ease in plain withdrawal. Those with understanding had means to see his mind.

sentences.zh: 楷今委頓，臣深憂之。

translations.literal: Kai is now worn down, and I am deeply worried about him.
translations.idiomatic: Kai is now worn down, and I am deeply worried about him.

sentences.zh: 光祿勳缺，以為可用。

translations.literal: The office of Chamberlain for the Splendid Blessings is vacant, and I think he can be used there.
translations.idiomatic: The office of Chamberlain for the Splendid Blessings is vacant, and I think he can be used there.

sentences.zh: 今張華在中書，王戎在尚書，足舉其契，無為復令楷入，名臣不多，當見將養，不違其志，要其遠濟之益。」

translations.literal: Now Zhang Hua is in the Palace Secretariat, and Wang Rong is in the Department of State Affairs; they are enough to raise what fits. There is no need to make Kai enter again. Eminent ministers are not many, and he should be cared for and nourished, without violating his will, so as to seek his long-range benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhang Hua is in the Palace Secretariat, and Wang Rong is in the Department of State Affairs; they are enough to raise what fits. There is no need to make Kai enter again. Eminent ministers are not many, and he should be cared for and nourished, without violating his will, so as to seek his long-range benefit."

sentences.zh: 不聽，就加光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: [The emperor] did not listen; [Kai] was additionally given Household Grandee and allowed to maintain a separate headquarters with ceremony equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: The throne instead piled on Household Grandee and three-duke parity.

sentences.zh: 及疾篤，詔遣黃門郎王衍省疾，楷回眸矚之曰：「竟未相識。」

translations.literal: When his illness became severe, the edict sent Yellow Gate Gentleman Wang Yan to inspect his illness. Kai turned his eyes back and gazed at him, saying, "In the end, we never came to know one another."
translations.idiomatic: When his illness became severe, the edict sent Yellow Gate Gentleman Wang Yan to inspect his illness. Kai turned his eyes back and gazed at him, saying, "In the end, we never came to know one another."

sentences.zh: 衍深歎其神俊。

translations.literal: Yan deeply sighed at his spiritual brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: Yan stood awed by that dying brilliance.

sentences.zh: 楷有知人之鑒，初在河南，樂廣僑居郡界，未知名，楷見而奇之，致之於宰府。

translations.literal: Kai had a gift for judging men; when first in Henan, Yue Guang sojourned within the commandery and was not yet known—Kai saw him, thought him extraordinary, and introduced him to the minister's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He discovered Yue Guang before fame.

sentences.zh: 嘗目夏侯玄云「肅肅如入宗廟中，但見禮樂器」，鍾會「如觀武庫森森，但見矛戟在前」，傅嘏「汪翔靡所不見」，山濤「若登山臨下，幽然深遠」。

translations.literal: He once judged Xiahou Xuan, saying, "Grave and reverent, as if entering the ancestral temple, where one sees only vessels for ritual and music"; Zhong Hui, "as if viewing an arsenal thickly arrayed, where one sees only spears and halberds in front"; Fu Gu, "vast and soaring, with nothing he does not see"; and Shan Tao, "like climbing a mountain and looking down, deep and distant in quietness."
translations.idiomatic: He once judged Xiahou Xuan, saying, "Grave and reverent, as if entering the ancestral temple, where one sees only vessels for ritual and music"; Zhong Hui, "as if viewing an arsenal thickly arrayed, where one sees only spears and halberds in front"; Fu Gu, "vast and soaring, with nothing he does not see"; and Shan Tao, "like climbing a mountain and looking down, deep and distant in quietness."

sentences.zh: 初，楷家炊黍在甑，或變如拳，或作血，或作蕪菁子。

translations.literal: At first, millet was steaming in Kai's kitchen steamer; some [grains] changed to fist shapes, some to blood, some to turnip seeds.
translations.idiomatic: Omens spoiled his grain—fists, blood, turnip seeds.

sentences.zh: 其年而卒，時年五十五，諡曰元。

translations.literal: That year he died, aged fifty-five; posthumous title Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died the same year at fifty-five as Marquis Yuan.

sentences.zh: 有五子：輿、瓚、憲、禮、遜。

translations.literal: He had five sons: Yu, Zan, Xian, Li, Xun.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Yu, Zan, Xian, Li, and Xun.

sentences.zh: 輿字祖明。

translations.literal: Yu, courtesy name Zuming.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yu bore the style Zuming.

sentences.zh: 少襲父爵，官至散騎侍郎，卒諡曰簡。

translations.literal: In youth he inherited his father's noble rank; he reached Supernumerary Gentleman of the Palace and died; posthumous title Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded early, died as supernumerary gentleman Jian.

sentences.zh: 瓚字國寶，中書郎，風神高邁，見者皆敬之。

translations.literal: Zan, courtesy name Guobao, was Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat; his bearing was lofty and transcendent; all who saw him revered him.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao Zan awed onlookers from the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 特為王綏所重，每從其遊。

translations.literal: Wang Sui especially esteemed him and constantly accompanied him on outings.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sui constantly shadowed Zan.

sentences.zh: 綏父戎謂之曰：「國寶初不來，汝數往，何也？」

translations.literal: Sui's father Rong said to him: "Guobao never comes to you—why do you go to him so often?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong wondered why Sui chased a host who never called."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「國寶雖不知綏，綏自知國寶。」

translations.literal: [Sui] replied: "Though Guobao does not know Sui, Sui knows Guobao."
translations.idiomatic: He need not notice me," Sui said, "I notice him."

sentences.zh: 楊駿之誅，為亂兵所害。=

translations.literal: When Yang Jun was executed, [Zan] was killed by mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's purge left Zan dead among the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 楷子憲

translations.literal: Kai's son Xian
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xian

sentences.zh: =憲字景思。

translations.literal: Xian, courtesy name Jingsi.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xian, style Jingsi,

sentences.zh: 少而穎悟，好交輕俠。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever and perceptive; he loved association and light chivalry.
translations.idiomatic: Brilliant boy, he chased gallantry.

sentences.zh: 及弱冠，更折節嚴重，修尚儒學，足不逾閾者數年。

translations.literal: By adulthood he had reformed to solemn dignity and cultivated Confucian learning; for several years his feet did not cross the threshold.
translations.idiomatic: He sobered into scholarship and stayed home.

sentences.zh: 陳郡謝鯤、潁川庾敳皆俊郎士也，見而奇之，相謂曰：「裴憲鯁亮宏達，通機識命，不知其何如父；

translations.literal: Xie Kun of Chen Commandery and Yu Ai of Yingchuan were both handsome young gentlemen. Seeing Xian, they considered him remarkable and said to one another, "Pei Xian is upright, bright, broad, and penetrating, understands opportunities, and knows the mandate. We do not know how he compares with his father;
translations.idiomatic: Xie Kun of Chen Commandery and Yu Ai of Yingchuan were both handsome young gentlemen. Seeing Xian, they considered him remarkable and said to one another, "Pei Xian is upright, bright, broad, and penetrating, understands opportunities, and knows the mandate. We do not know how he compares with his father;

sentences.zh: 至於深弘保素，不以世物嬰心者，其殆過之。」

translations.literal: but as for being deep and broad, preserving plainness, and not letting worldly things entangle his mind, he probably surpasses him."
translations.idiomatic: but as for being deep and broad, preserving plainness, and not letting worldly things entangle his mind, he probably surpasses him."

sentences.zh: 初，侍講東宮，曆黃門吏部郎、侍中。

translations.literal: At first he lectured in the Eastern Palace and successively served as Huangmen, Director of Personnel, and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from tutor through Huangmen and personnel to attendant.

sentences.zh: 東海王越以為豫州刺史、北中郎將、假節。

translations.literal: Prince Donghai Yue made him Governor of Yuzhou, General Who Pacifies the North, and Bearer of Staff of Authority.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue sent him to Yuzhou as northern commander with staff.

sentences.zh: 王浚承制，以憲為尚書。

translations.literal: Wang Jun by imperial mandate made Xian Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun's mandate elevated him to minister.

sentences.zh: 永嘉末，王浚為石勒所破，棗嵩等莫不謝罪軍門，貢賂交錯，惟憲及荀綽恬然私室。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongjia, Wang Jun was broken by Shi Le; Zao Song and the rest all apologized at the army gate with tribute crisscrossing—only Xian and Xun Chuo remained tranquil in private chambers.
translations.idiomatic: When Le crushed Jun, officials rushed to abase themselves—Xian and Xun Chuo stayed dignified.

sentences.zh: 勒素聞其名，召而謂之曰：「王浚虐暴幽州，人鬼同疾。

translations.literal: Le had long heard of his reputation, summoned him, and said to him, "Wang Jun was cruel and violent in Youzhou, and humans and spirits alike hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Le had long heard of his reputation, summoned him, and said to him, "Wang Jun was cruel and violent in Youzhou, and humans and spirits alike hated him.

sentences.zh: 孤恭行乾憲，拯茲黎元，羈舊咸歡，慶謝交路。

translations.literal: I respectfully carry out the heavenly constitution and rescue these common people; old dependents and captives are all rejoicing, and celebrations and thanks fill the roads.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully carry out the heavenly constitution and rescue these common people; old dependents and captives are all rejoicing, and celebrations and thanks fill the roads.

sentences.zh: 二君齊惡傲威，誠信岨絕，防風之戮，將誰歸乎？」

translations.literal: You two gentlemen join him in evil and are arrogant toward authority; sincerity and trust are cut off and blocked. To whom will the execution of Fangfeng return?"
translations.idiomatic: You two gentlemen join him in evil and are arrogant toward authority; sincerity and trust are cut off and blocked. To whom will the execution of Fangfeng return?"

sentences.zh: 憲神色侃然，泣而對曰：「臣等世荷晉榮，恩遇隆重。

translations.literal: Xian's expression was composed, and he wept as he replied, "We have for generations borne Jin glory, and its grace and treatment have been deep and weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's expression was composed, and he wept as he replied, "We have for generations borne Jin glory, and its grace and treatment have been deep and weighty.

sentences.zh: 王浚凶粗醜正，尚晉之遺籓。

translations.literal: Wang Jun is fierce, coarse, and hostile to the correct, but he still is a surviving regional lord of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun is fierce, coarse, and hostile to the correct, but he still is a surviving regional lord of Jin.

sentences.zh: 雖欣聖化，義岨誠心。

translations.literal: Although I rejoice in sagely transformation, righteousness blocks my sincere heart.
translations.idiomatic: Although I rejoice in sagely transformation, righteousness blocks my sincere heart.

sentences.zh: 且武王伐紂，表商容之閭，未聞商容在倒戈之例也。

translations.literal: Moreover, when King Wu attacked Zhou, he marked the lane of Shang Rong; I have not heard that Shang Rong was placed among those who reversed their spears.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when King Wu attacked Zhou, he marked the lane of Shang Rong; I have not heard that Shang Rong was placed among those who reversed their spears.

sentences.zh: 明公既不欲以道化厲物，必于刑忍為治者，防風之戮，臣之分也。

translations.literal: If Your Enlightened Lordship does not wish to transform and encourage things by the Way, but must make governance through punishment and cruelty, then Fangfeng's execution is my allotment.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Enlightened Lordship does not wish to transform and encourage things by the Way, but must make governance through punishment and cruelty, then Fangfeng's execution is my allotment.

sentences.zh: 請就辟有司。」

translations.literal: I request to go before the responsible officers for punishment."
translations.idiomatic: I request to go before the responsible officers for punishment."

sentences.zh: 不拜而出。

translations.literal: He refused appointment and walked out.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the post and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 勒深嘉之，待以賓禮。

translations.literal: Le praised him deeply and treated him with the courtesy due a guest.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le honored him as a guest.

sentences.zh: 勒乃簿王浚官寮親屬，皆貲至巨萬，惟憲與荀綽家有書百餘帙，鹽米各十數斛而已。

translations.literal: Le then audited Wang Jun's officials and kin—all had piled treasure to the tens of millions; only Xian and Xun Chuo had households with a hundred-odd bundles of books and only several dozen hu each of salt and rice.
translations.idiomatic: Le inventoried Jun's corrupt circle—only Xian and Chuo owned books and handfuls of grain instead of piled gold.

sentences.zh: 勒聞之，謂其長史張賓曰：「名不虛也。

translations.literal: When Le heard of this, he said to his Chief Clerk Zhang Bin, "Their names are not empty.
translations.idiomatic: When Le heard of this, he said to his Chief Clerk Zhang Bin, "Their names are not empty.

sentences.zh: 吾不喜得幽州，喜獲二子。」

translations.literal: I do not rejoice at obtaining Youzhou; I rejoice at obtaining these two men."
translations.idiomatic: I do not rejoice at obtaining Youzhou; I rejoice at obtaining these two men."

sentences.zh: 署從事中郎，出為長樂太守。

translations.literal: He appointed him attendant for executive affairs and sent him out as Governor of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Le named him staff adviser and governor of Changle.

sentences.zh: 及勒僭號，未遑制度，與王波為之撰朝儀，於是憲章文物，擬于王者。

translations.literal: When Le assumed a usurping title, before institutions were in place, he and Wang Bo drafted court ritual for him, whereupon statutes, regalia, and implements rivaled a true king's.
translations.idiomatic: When Later Zhao began court ritual, Xian and Wang Bo drafted ceremonies fit for emperors.

sentences.zh: 勒大悅，署太中大夫，遷司徒。

translations.literal: Le was greatly pleased, appointed him Grand Palace Counselor, then Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Le made him grand counselor, then minister of education.

sentences.zh: 及季龍之世，彌加禮重。

translations.literal: Under Shihu's reign he received still greater ritual honor.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu later elevated him further.

sentences.zh: 憲有二子：挹、㲄，並以文才知名。

translations.literal: Xian had two sons, Yi and Gu, both famed for literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and Gu inherited literary fame.

sentences.zh: 㲄仕季龍為太子中庶子、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Gu served under Shihu as Palace Mentor to the heir apparent and Supernumerary Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Gu advised Shi Hu's heir as household tutor.

sentences.zh: 挹、㲄俱豪俠耽酒，好臧否人物。

translations.literal: Yi and Gu were both swaggering bravos who drank deep and loved judging character aloud.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers drank, swaggered, and gossiped about peers.

sentences.zh: 與河間邢魚有隙，魚竊乘㲄馬奔段遼，為人所獲，魚誣㲄使己以季龍當襲鮮卑，告之為備。

translations.literal: They feuded with Xing Yu of Hejian; Yu stole Gu's horse and fled to Duan Liao, was captured, and falsely claimed Gu had sent him to warn that Shihu would soon strike the Xianbei so they should prepare.
translations.idiomatic: A stolen horse and Xing Yu's lie framed them before Duan Liao.

sentences.zh: 時季龍適謀伐遼，而與魚辭正合。

translations.literal: At the moment Shihu was indeed plotting a campaign against Liao, and Yu's story matched his suspicions.
translations.idiomatic: Hu's planned Xianbei war lent credence to the forgery.

sentences.zh: 季龍悉誅挹、㲄，憲亦坐免。

translations.literal: Shihu executed both Yi and Gu; Xian also lost office as implicated.
translations.idiomatic: Hu purged both sons and cashiered Xian.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復以為右光祿大夫、司徒、太傅，封安定郡公。

translations.literal: Before long Xian was again appointed Right Household Grandee, Minister of Education, and Grand Tutor, enfeoffed Duke of Anding commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as household grandee, minister, tutor, and duke of Anding.

sentences.zh: 憲曆官無干績之稱，然在朝玄默，未嘗以物務經懷。

translations.literal: Though Xian earned no reputation for administrative feats in successive posts, at court he remained silent and never let mundane tasks burden his heart.
translations.idiomatic: He governed quietly without bustle while minds praised his virtue.

sentences.zh: 但以德重名高，動見尊禮。

translations.literal: Yet by the weight of his virtue and fame he was everywhere received with deferential ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Reputation alone won him ritual honor.

sentences.zh: 竟卒于石氏，以族人峙子邁為嗣。

translations.literal: In the end he died under the Shi clan; his clansman Zhi's son Mai was appointed heir.
translations.idiomatic: He died under Shi rule; cousin Mai continued the line.

sentences.zh: 楷長兄黎，次兄康，並知名。

translations.literal: Kai's eldest brother Li and middle brother Kang were both celebrated.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Li and Pei Kang matched their fame.

sentences.zh: 康子盾，少曆顯位。

translations.literal: Kang's son Dun in youth held prominent offices.
translations.idiomatic: Kang's son Dun rose fast.

sentences.zh: 永嘉中，為徐州刺史，委任長史司馬奧。

translations.literal: During Yongjia he was Governor of Xuzhou, leaving affairs to his chief clerk Sima Ao.
translations.idiomatic: As Xuzhou governor he delegated to Sima Ao.

sentences.zh: 奧勸盾刑殺立威，大發良人為兵，有不奉法者罪便至死。

translations.literal: Ao urged Dun to instill awe through executions and conscripted commoners as soldiers in huge numbers; anyone who violated regulations faced death.
translations.idiomatic: Ao's terror tactics—mass levies and capital punishment—ruled Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 在任三年，百姓嗟怨。

translations.literal: Within three years the common people groaned with resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years the people cursed them.

sentences.zh: 東海王越，盾妹夫也。

translations.literal: Prince Donghai Yue was Dun's brother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Donghai Wang Yue was Dun's brother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 越既薨，騎督滿衡便引所發良人東還。

translations.literal: After Yue died, Cavalry Commander Man Heng led the conscripted commoners eastward.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue died Man Heng marched the levies east.

sentences.zh: 尋而劉元海遣將王桑、趙固向彭城，前鋒數騎至下邳，文武不堪苛政，悉皆散走，盾、奧奔淮陰，妻子為賊人所得。

translations.literal: Soon Liu Yuanhai sent generals Wang Sang and Zhao Gu toward Pengcheng; a handful of vanguard riders reached Xiapi—the officials could not endure the harsh rule and scattered; Dun and Ao fled to Huaiyin, and their wives and children were seized by raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan's vanguard reached Xiapi; officials fled harsh rule; Dun fled to Huaiyin and lost family to bandits.

sentences.zh: 奧又誘盾降趙固。

translations.literal: Ao also induced Dun to surrender to Zhao Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Ao pushed Dun toward Zhao Gu.

sentences.zh: 固妻盾女，有寵，盾向女涕泣，固遂殺之。

translations.literal: Gu's wife was Dun's daughter and enjoyed his favor; Dun wept to his daughter, whereupon Gu killed her.
translations.idiomatic: Gu slew Dun's daughter—his own wife—after Dun's tearful plea.

sentences.zh: 盾弟邵，字道期。

translations.literal: Dun's younger brother Shao, courtesy name Daoqi.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Shao, style Daoqi.

sentences.zh: 元帝為安東將軍，以邵為長史，王導為司馬，二人相與為深交。

translations.literal: When Yuan-di served as General of the East, he appointed Shao chief clerk alongside Wang Dao as chief administrator—the two became sworn friends.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuan-di Shao served with Wang Dao as the prince's twin pillars.

sentences.zh: 徵為太子中庶子，復轉散騎常侍，使持節、都督揚州江西淮北諸軍事、東中郎將，隨越出項，而卒於軍中。

translations.literal: Shao was summoned as mentor to the heir, then made Supernumerary Palace Attendant, Bearer of Staff, Area Commander of all military affairs west of the Yangzi and north of the Huai in Yangzhou, and General of the East Center; he followed Yue to Xiang and died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: He died with Yue's army after tutor and Yangzhou commands.

sentences.zh: 及王導為司空，既拜，歎曰：「裴道期、劉王喬在，吾不得獨登此位。」

translations.literal: When Wang Dao became Minister of Works, after he had received the appointment, he sighed and said, "If Pei Daoqi and Liu Wangqiao were alive, I could not have ascended this position alone."
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dao became Minister of Works, after he had received the appointment, he sighed and said, "If Pei Daoqi and Liu Wangqiao were alive, I could not have ascended this position alone."

sentences.zh: 導子仲豫與康同字，導思舊好，乃改為敬豫焉。

translations.literal: Dao's son Zhongyu shared Kang's courtesy name; Dao, cherishing old ties, renamed him Jingyu.
translations.idiomatic: Dao renamed a son to avoid clashing with Pei Kang's style.

sentences.zh: 楷弟綽，字季舒，器宇宏曠，官至黃門侍郎、長水校尉。

translations.literal: Kai's younger brother Chuo, courtesy name Jishu, had a vast, open manner and rose to Palace Attendant and Colonel of the Long River Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo rose to palace gates and the Long River corps.

sentences.zh: 綽子遐，善言玄理，音辭清暢，泠然若琴瑟。

translations.literal: Chuo's son Xia excelled at expounding arcane principles; his tone was lucid and flowing, cool and pure as zithers and lutes.
translations.idiomatic: Xia's qingtan equaled music in clarity.

sentences.zh: 嘗與河南郭象談論，一坐嗟服。

translations.literal: Once he debated Guo Xiang of Henan—the whole assembly sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: He once silenced a hall debating Guo Xiang.

sentences.zh: 又嘗在平東將軍周馥坐，與人圍棋。

translations.literal: Again, seated with General Pacifying the East Zhou Fu, he was playing weiqi with another.
translations.idiomatic: At Pacifying the East Zhou Fu's headquarters he played weiqi with companions.

sentences.zh: 馥司馬行酒，遐未即飲，司馬醉怒，因曳遐墮地。

translations.literal: Fu's major passed the wine; Xia did not drink immediately; the major, drunk and furious, dragged Xia and threw him down.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu's major passed wine, Xia hesitated; drunk and furious, the man dragged him from the mat.

sentences.zh: 遐徐起還坐，顏色不變，復棋如故。

translations.literal: Xia slowly rose, returned to his seat, his color unchanged, and resumed the game.
translations.idiomatic: He rose slowly, resumed his seat without changing color, and continued the game.

sentences.zh: 其性虛和如此。

translations.literal: His temperament was mild and yielding to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: His cool temper matched his metaphysics.

sentences.zh: 東海王越引為主簿，後為越子毗所害。

translations.literal: Prince Donghai Yue took him as chief clerk; later Yue's son Pi murdered him.
translations.idiomatic: Donghai heir Pi executed him.

sentences.zh: 初，裴、王二族盛于魏晉之世，時人以為八裴方八王：徽比王祥，楷比王衍，康比王綏，綽比王澄，瓚比王敦，遐比王導，頠比王戎，邈比王玄雲。

translations.literal: At first the Pei and Wang houses flourished side by side in the Wei-Jin age; contemporaries likened eight Peis to eight Wangs: Wei to Wang Xiang, Kai to Wang Yan, Kang to Wang Sui, Chuo to Wang Cheng, Zan to Wang Dun, Xia to Wang Dao, Yi to Wang Rong, and Miao to Wang Xuanyun.
translations.idiomatic: Wei-Jin society paired eight Peis with eight Wangs like paired stars.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historian's appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Section heading for editorial judgement.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：周稱多士，漢曰得人，取類星象，頡頏符契。

translations.literal: The historians say: Zhou praised "many shi"; Han spoke of "gaining men"—they classified types like constellations and matched tally halves.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin historians compare worthy ministers to Zhou's host of talents and Han's knack for personnel.

sentences.zh: 時乏名流，多以幹翮相許，自家光國，豈陳騫之謂歟！

translations.literal: When distinguished figures were few, men mostly traded praise of administrative talent—thinking to glorify house and state—is this not precisely what Chen Qian meant!
translations.idiomatic: They hint Chen Qian embodied vain ministerial boasting.

sentences.zh: 秀則聲蓋朋僚，稱為領袖。

translations.literal: As for Xiu, his voice overshadowed peers and he was called their leader.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xiu led his generation.

sentences.zh: 楷則機神幼發，目以清通。

translations.literal: As for Kai, wit and spirit stirred early and observers dubbed him lucid and penetrating.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Kai earned his reputation for enlightened clarity.

sentences.zh: 俱為晉氏名臣，良有以也。

translations.literal: Together they stood as Jin's celebrated ministers—and rightly so.
translations.idiomatic: They deserved Jin's esteem.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：世既順才，才膺世至。

translations.literal: The encomium runs: The age bows to talent; talent rises to meet the age.
translations.idiomatic: The verse praises timely union of talent and age.

sentences.zh: 高平沈敏，蘊茲名器。

translations.literal: Gaoping's Chen Qian was deep and astute, cherishing those vessels of fame.
translations.idiomatic: It salutes Chen Qian's steady grasp of power.

sentences.zh: 钜鹿自然，亦云經笥。

translations.literal: Julu's Pei Xiu moved with natural ease—another walking library of the classics.
translations.idiomatic: It salutes Pei Xiu's effortless scholarship.

sentences.zh: 媧皇煉石，晉圖開秘。

translations.literal: The goddess Nüwa smelted stone to mend heaven; Jin's charts unlocked hidden treasure.
translations.idiomatic: It invokes myth and charts to praise Jin mapping.

sentences.zh: 頠有清規，承家來媚。

translations.literal: Yi upheld pure standards, inheriting grace for his house.
translations.idiomatic: It closes by honoring Pei Yi's integrity.
